shapes.name: runtime_safety_off_and_977_reduction
shapes.reason: fe_mul median stayed 14 ns. ReleaseSafe fe_mul is 604 bytes with 24 mul and 22 umulh and no library call; the reduction is three widening multiplies by 0x1000003d1, not a loop. @setRuntimeSafety(false) left that object the same size, because the widening product cannot overflow. A straight-line multiply by 977 plus a 32-bit shift was correct against the division test and was 372 bytes with 16 mul and 16 umulh in isolation, but in the node bench fe_inv moved 740 to 1253 ns, point_double 89 to 112 ns, and ecdsa_verify 37202 to 40910 ns. Reverted.
shapes.tests_before_bench: test-crypto-vectors and test-crypto-mutations passed on the candidate; those artifacts were not indexed because the shape was reverted

shapes.name: fixed_window_g
shapes.reason: Width-16 fixed windows for G and lambda*G are already the committed schedule, 16384 affine points each, 2097152 bytes together. ECDSA verify already records 68 table hits, 127 doublings, and 1950 field multiplications. Building that table at first use would not change the verify count, so it was not rebuilt and the embed stays.

residual: Field multiplication stays 14 ns and 1950 operations, 96 percent of ECDSA verify. Turning runtime safety off and replacing the widening complement multiply with a 977-and-shift reduction did not lower fe_mul and slowed fe_inv and verify, so it was reverted. The committed schedule is already a width-16 fixed window for G, a width-4 wNAF for P, and a four-term GLV joint chain at about 128 doublings. A magnitude-tracked 5x52 multiply measured 72 ns against this u256 multiply.
